features.title: Open the manager for skills, MCP servers or plugins from one page
features.summary: Settings › Capabilities hub lists the three kinds of capability an agent or DSH can gain: skills (agent instructions), MCP servers (tools and credentials) and DSH plugins (executable code), each with its own trust label, a read-only count from its owner (the dshx registry's skills, the MCP servers list, the plugin inventory) and a button that opens that owner's page. Skills also link out to skills.sh and offer a copyable install command with telemetry off and a pinned CLI version; DSH never runs it. The hub stores nothing, installs nothing and makes no network call. The capabilities_hub_overview agent tool returns the same routing and guidance.
features.currentSurface: rail: Settings › Capabilities hub (already on the rail)
failureModes: A manager page that is not loaded keeps its card with a disabled Open button and names the package to add to the profile.
An owner API that is absent shows which plugin the count needs instead of a number.
skills.sh search needs a Vercel OIDC login DSH cannot hold, so the hub links to the site instead of searching in place.

externalDependencies.boundary: A plain link to https://skills.sh and a copyable `npx skills@<pinned> add` command with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1; the plugin makes no request to skills.sh and runs no CLI.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: None needed: src/hub-panel.test.tsx asserts the link target and the copied command.

features.title: Open the plugin market from Settings
features.summary: Settings › Plugin Market frames the catalog section the dshmarket plugin registers, the same section All settings lists, as a stage page beside the managers it fills. With no market plugin loaded the page names the install command and fills in once the section registers; it stores nothing itself and makes no network call.
failureModes: With no plugin registering the market section the page keeps its Settings row and names the install command instead of rendering an empty frame.
The catalog's own load failures stay inside the section it owns; the page only frames it.

externalDependencies.boundary: A settings section registered by the installed dshmarket bundle; the page renders that section and never calls the catalog or npm itself.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/plugin-market-page.test.tsx renders a stub section for the loaded case and the install hint for the missing one.

telemetry.reason: Client-only: the page frames a settings section another plugin registers and starts no Host work of its own.
